The test image shows a split-open corn stalk with shredded, macerated pith leaving stringy vascular strands. Tan/brown coloration. This is a **stem** disease.

Stem candidates: Anthracnose, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Purple_Leaf_Sheath, Common_Smut, others.

Top suspects based on the shredded pith with vascular strands: Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot. Let me view references one at a time, starting with one from each top candidate.
Charcoal stalk rot reference shows shredded pith with dark sclerotia visible. Similar shredding pattern to test image. Let me check Diplodia_Stalk_Rot next.
Diplodia shows stalk breakage at node but not the same shredded internal appearance. Let me check Bacterial_Stalk_Rot.
Bacterial stalk rot looks very different - external view with water-soaked discoloration. Let me check Anthracnose (stem) and Physoderma_Stalk_Rot.
Anthracnose stem shows dark black lesions on the rind exterior and some internal shredding, with pinkish-red discoloration. Different from the test image. Let me check Physoderma_Stalk_Rot.
Physoderma stalk rot shows dark spots on green stalk - completely different. Let me check Purple_Leaf_Sheath.

Purple_Leaf_Sheath shows dark lesions on green stalk exterior - completely different. Let me check another Diplodia_Stalk_Rot reference and another Charcoal_Stalk_Rot to compare these two top candidates more carefully.

This Charcoal_Stalk_Rot reference shows much darker, more severely charred-looking shredded stalks with grey/black coloration. The test image is lighter tan/brown without the characteristic charred appearance. Let me use my last view on another Diplodia_Stalk_Rot reference.

Now I have all 8 views. Let me synthesize:

**Test image**: Split-open corn stalk with completely shredded/macerated pith, leaving only stringy vascular strands. Light tan/brown coloration. Photographed on dark background.

**Comparison**:
- **Charcoal_Stalk_Rot** (ref 1): Very similar shredding pattern with pith decomposed into stringy vascular strands. The first reference showed a similar light tan color in the upper portion. The hallmark of charcoal stalk rot is exactly this: "shredded stalks with rotted pith leaving only stringy vascular strands."
- **Diplodia_Stalk_Rot**: References showed external stalk breakage at nodes and pycnidia on rind, not the same internal shredding pattern.
- **Bacterial_Stalk_Rot**: Shows soft, mushy water-soaked tissue, not shredded.
- **Anthracnose**: Shows dark black external lesions with reddish discoloration.
- **Physoderma/Purple_Leaf_Sheath**: Show spots on green stalks, completely different.

The shredded pith with only stringy vascular strands remaining is the diagnostic feature of Charcoal_Stalk_Rot. While the test image is lighter than the most severe charcoal rot examples, the first reference showed a very similar appearance, and no other candidate matches this shredding pattern.
